thread:
incident-bot: Pager alert fired for service=frontend-network, reason=ALB target health spike + TLS handshake failures. PD: https://pagerduty.example/incident/PD12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Trigger: frontend-network (prod) — High error rate on ALB targets. Acknowledgement required. Incident priority P1.

emma: acked — I'm on call. jumping in. @sachin can you pull ALB target health?

sachin: looking. seeing a flurry of `502`/`524` from edge and `TLS handshake` errors in the ALB logs. Also backend target health showing a lot of "unhealthy" for tg-frontend-prod-us-east-1.

emma: any config changes/deploys in last 10m?

sachin: not from our side. quick grep in deploy logs shows no recent rollouts. Could be cert rotation or upstream OS update. grabbing `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:...` now.

netops-bot: Auto-check summary: DNS to api.redwood-inference.com resolved to ALB-a + ALB-b; ALB-a target group unhealthy 72% unhealthy, ALB-b healthy. TLS handshake failure rate 18% over last 5m (SNI mismatch / handshake timeout).

sachin: paste snippet from elbv2: ```
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    {"Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.34"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "TLSHandshakeFailure"}},
    {"Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.35"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "healthy"}}
  ]
}
```

emma: ok. initial hypothesis: ALB-a has unhealthy targets causing increased TLS handshake failures (maybe expired cert or misconfig on a subset of nodes). Impacting ~15% of inbound requests (based on edge telemetry).

liam: echoing — I can flip traffic to eu-backup if we need immediate mitigation, but prefer to try quick target rotation first to recover capacity in us-east.

emma: plan: 1) remove unhealthy targets from ALB-a to stop routing to them 2) register replacement targets (warm hosts) 3) if the error rate doesn't drop in 3m, fail traffic to ALB-b / weighted Route53 to eu-backup. sachin, can you remove/regenerate?

sachin: on it. commands: ```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=10.0.12.34
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=10.0.12.99
```
Doing that now.

netops-bot: Deregister request accepted. New target 10.0.12.99 starting health checks.

sachin: new target warmed and showing healthy. ALB-a healthy count up to 65% from 28% in 90s. TLS handshake failures trending down.

emma: good. metrics: errors down from ~18% to ~4% in the last 2 minutes. still seeing a couple of TLS timeouts from legacy clients.

liam: I'm going to prepare a failover runbook if we need it. Route53 weight on api.redwood-inference.com can shift 20% to eu-backup immediately. TTL is 60s.

emma: please hold on failover — continue to monitor 5m window. sachin, can you check cert expiry on those replaced hosts? ```
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.99:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
```

sachin: certs look fine on the new hosts. expiry 2027-01-10. The unhealthy hosts return a client handshake timeout; their kernel tcp retrans counters are high. I suspect kernel-level drop after recent kernel livepatch we rolled earlier today on a subset of hosts.

emma: that matches timeline. Ops change rollback? Who pushed the livepatch?

liam: infra schedule shows a kernel micro-update at 2162499800 (20m before alert) targeting a canary subset. Seems the canary made it to prod in error. ops team notified.

emma: action: roll back the livepatch on affected hosts, cordon them from ALB and recreate. sachin, continue to pull unhealthy nodes; liam, initiate rollback with infra. I'll update PD incident notes and customers.

sachin: rolling back on hosts 10.0.12.34/35/36 now. deregistering fully.```

netops-bot: Health now: ALB-a healthy targets 88%. TLS handshake failure rate 0.9% last 1m.

emma: nice. customer impact estimate: peak ~15% request failures for ~8 minutes, affecting some real-time generation requests; POST/stream endpoints saw highest errors. No data leakage suspected. Creating incident timeline in docs: https://docs.internal/incidents/INC-2162500000

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 acknowledged by emma. Escalation paused.

liam: infra rollback confirmed complete. affected hosts restarted and re-joined, health checks ok. moving traffic back gradually.

emma: I'm going to hand off monitoring to liam for the next 45m while I finish customer comms. liam, please escalate if errors creep above 2%.

liam: ack — I'll monitor dashboards and alerts. setting PD rule to page me at >2% TLS handshake errors for 5m.

sachin: leaving a short note in runbook: "avoid auto-propagating livepatch canary to all hosts — ensure tag-based scoping". filing a follow-up with infra.

emma: thanks all. summary: root cause likely inadvertent kernel livepatch applied to subset of ALB targets, causing TLS handshake timeouts. mitigation: deregister bad targets, register warmed replacements, rollback patch. customer impact limited and largely recovered. closing on-call active mitigation.

liam: closing monitoring handoff — will post final status in 45m or earlier. :white_check_mark:
